faqs.q: How many radians are in a degree?
faqs.a: π/180 ≈ 0.0174533 radians per degree. A full circle is 2π radians = 360°.
Gradians divide a right angle into 100 parts, so a full circle is 400 gradians. They are still used in some surveying work.
Artillery and military optics divide the circle into 6,400 NATO mils, so 1 mil ≈ 0.05625°. It is handy because 1 mil subtends about 1 m at 1 km.
